A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, with matching authors, taxonomy and methodological sections. All pages, including Appendix A in each version, are readable; the text, rendered figures and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original descriptive analysis of the surveyed literature, including publication counts in Figure 1 and an analysis of 315 papers in Section 5.3 reporting 75.5% recovery versus 24.5% non-recovery methods.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the authors' recovery and missingness statistics and adds annual counts by methodological category in Figure 18 and Section 5.4. These constitute original data-analysis results, although no model benchmarking experiments are conducted.

M1.justification: The two-aspect, four-type, twelve-category taxonomy remains unchanged. Newly discussed methods such as SensorGAN, MultiPro and FedMobile belong to cited research; the survey does not introduce or modify a proposed learning algorithm.

E1.justification: The expanded medical and pervasive-computing dataset catalogue in Table 3 and Section 6 describes resources used by other studies. Neither version conducts its own model training or evaluation on these datasets.

E2.justification: Neither version conducts model-baseline experiments. Tables 1 and 2 remain qualitative comparisons and classifications of existing method types; added literature citations are not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported literature collection changes from 315 papers spanning 2012–October 2024 to 354 spanning 2012–August 2025. The publication-count analysis extends to 2025, and Figure 18 introduces counting by year and methodological category. Section 5.3 still explicitly uses 315 papers; a wholesale reanalysis is not established.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Figure 18 examine methodological evolution through annual counts of four method categories. This supplements v3's aggregate publication trend and recovery/missingness breakdowns. No author-run ablation or sensor-robustness experiment is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive counts and percentages without repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 18 adds descriptive results using the existing reporting practice, without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 1 retains the 2014–2024 counts and adds 37 papers for 2025. Figure 18 introduces category-by-year results, although its 2024 stack totals 59 versus 64 in Figure 1. The existing recovery and missing-rate percentages remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs or derivations, and the mathematical content of the shared method descriptions is retained. New discussion of complementarity, learned priors and theoretical gaps is conceptual rather than new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: a comprehensive deep-MLMM survey, a fine-grained taxonomy, and analysis of methods, datasets, applications and future directions. Broader literature coverage supports these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands interpretation through technical-evolution discussion, realistic and asynchronous sensor failures, temporal alignment, modality complementarity, and data-scale confounds in comparisons. Sections 7–8 also explicitly qualify the taxonomy's practical rather than theoretical scope and its possible obsolescence as foundation models evolve.

D1.justification: v4 adds dataset access information, including the TCGA portal in Table 3 and mBrain21 and UCI dataset locators in the references. The collection description and Appendix A also add TMLR to the source venues. No implementation or experimental reproduction package is introduced.

R1.justification: The literature review expands substantially into wearable and IoT sensing, mobile federated learning, computational pathology, and gene/cell representation learning. Newly integrated examples include SensorGAN, FedMobile, MultiPro, DeepLIIF and HE2RNA. These extend the survey's research context beyond citation-format or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are tightened, application headings are renamed, and technical-evolution, pervasive-computing and practical-missingness subsections are added. Author affiliations and citation style also change. The eight main sections retain their order, and most existing methodological prose remains.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout from ACM styling to TMLR typography, headers, title block and reference layout. Figure 1 is extended, Figure 18 is new, Table 3 is expanded and compressed, and existing figures and tables shift relative to the text. Most methodological schematics are reused.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the survey more useful through broader sensing and biomedical coverage and more specific discussion of realistic missingness, temporal alignment, comparison confounds and taxonomy limitations. These gains in critical synthesis outweigh limited regressions, including the less legible Table 3 and the unexplained discrepancy between Figure 18's 2024 total of 59 and Figure 1's 64. The core taxonomy and most quantitative analyses remain unchanged.
